metadata.title: Distinguish resolver and authoritative responses
metadata.topic: DNS Operations — Offline Evidence (Simulator / Offline snapshots)

mission.brief: Separate DNS answers, negative responses and transport silence. Keep the first six records: context and five query outcomes, including flags and authority evidence. Save the required factual records in report.txt and display the final report with cat. Self-review the interpretation and next checks in HELP.txt.
constraints: SIMULATOR / OFFLINE SNAPSHOTS: fictional supplied evidence, not live measurements of your computer or VM. Read reference.txt for source excerpts and HELP.txt for context/model interpretation.
Automatic score checks exact factual report bytes (80) and final cat report.txt (20). Free-form reasoning, diagnoses and next checks are self-reviewed; 100/100 is not mastery.

Keep record spelling, order and final LF exactly; equivalent supported paths/filters are accepted, arbitrary report formatting is not normalized. Only report.txt is writable. > truncates first; failures do not undo writes. Finish all writes before the checked reading; any write clears prior reading evidence.

Challenge states the same factual requirements without a repair command. No service changes, live lookups, certificate validation, shell or network execution. Type help for supported commands; cat HELP.txt for this lesson reference.

hints: Compare the question with the supplied vantage points, timestamps and fields. Which responses deny a name, deny only the requested type, or contain no received response?

Read reference.txt and HELP.txt. RA advertises recursion availability; RD requests recursion, and AA marks an authoritative answer. The NOERROR/empty AAAA answer with authoritative SOA is negative type data (NODATA), not a nonexistent name. NXDOMAIN denies the queried name; SERVFAIL reports server failure without establishing its cause. A timeout has no received RCODE. A recursive non-AA response alone does not prove it came from cache. Select only the required records; do not add a causal conclusion to the scored factual report.
A supported construction is: head -n 6 evidence.txt > report.txt. Then cat report.txt. Interpret the result separately; this score checks facts and inspection only.

/home/learner/reference.txt.content:
Synthetic dig response excerpts at 09:00 UTC; query names/types and server accompany each normalized record.
Recursive query: status: NOERROR; flags: qr rd ra; ANSWER: 1; portal.example.test. 300 IN A 198.51.100.40

Authoritative +norecurse absent-name query: status: NXDOMAIN; flags: qr aa; ANSWER: 0; same SOA in authority.

/home/learner/HELP.txt.content:
SIMULATOR / OFFLINE SNAPSHOTS — Distinguish resolver and authoritative responses
Goal: Separate DNS answers, negative responses and transport silence.
These original synthetic annotated records describe fictional hosts, not your computer or a VM. reference.txt gives realistic source excerpts; evidence.txt contains normalized records for extraction, not literal tool output. No ip, ping, ss, dig, named-checkzone, curl, openssl, Apache or nginx command executes here.
Task: Keep the first six records: context and five query outcomes, including flags and authority evidence.
Report format: preserve the selected record spelling, order and final LF exactly. Equivalent supported filters and paths are accepted; alternative prose/formatting is not normalized. Only report.txt is writable. Finish every write before cat report.txt; a later write invalidates reading evidence. Type help for the bounded text-command syntax.
Automatically checked: report facts (80 points) and displaying that final report with cat (20 points). No points for reading every source. A 100/100 score is NOT verified diagnostic reasoning or operational mastery.
Self-review questions: Which responses deny a name, deny only the requested type, or contain no received response?
Model interpretation: RA advertises recursion availability; RD requests recursion, and AA marks an authoritative answer. The NOERROR/empty AAAA answer with authoritative SOA is negative type data (NODATA), not a nonexistent name. NXDOMAIN denies the queried name; SERVFAIL reports server failure without establishing its cause. A timeout has no received RCODE. A recursive non-AA response alone does not prove it came from cache.
Common mistakes: Calling every empty answer NXDOMAIN; treating timeout as SERVFAIL; reading RA as proof of authority or cached origin; blaming a network path from a DNS status alone.
Reasoning, proposed next checks and causal claims are self-reviewed, not keyword graded. Challenge hides guided commands and hints; this conceptual reference remains available.
Reset restores sources/reports and starts a new attempt, preserving history. Resume retains report, pending input, mode and exact scenario identity. This complements real practice; no live configuration or network effect occurs.
